question.worked_solution:
At $x=2,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}{2}^{bx} \\  & ={2}^{b(2)} \\  & ={2}^{2b},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}({x}^{2}+4) \\  & =(2)^{2}+4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}h(x) \\ {2}^{2b} & =8 \\ {2}^{2b} & ={2}^{3} \\ 2b & =3 \\ b & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
